L = ["██╗ ", "██║ ", "██║ ", "██║ ", "███████╗", "╚══════╝"] O = [" ██████╗ ", "██╔═══██╗", "██║ ██║", "██║ ██║", "╚██████╔╝", " ╚═════╝ "] C = [" ██████╗ ", "██╔════╝ ", "██║ ", "██║ ", "╚██████╗ ", " ╚═════╝ "] A = [" █████╗ ", "██╔══██╗ ", "███████║ ", "██╔══██║ ", "██║ ██║ ", "╚═╝ ╚═╝ "] I = ["██╗", "██║", "██║", "██║", "██║", "╚═╝"] for name, cell in [("L",L),("O",O),("C",C),("A",A),("I",I)]: ws = {len(r) for r in cell} assert len(ws) == 1 and len(cell) == 6, (name, ws) glifos = [L, O, C, A, L, C, L, I] filas = [" ".join(g[r] for g in glifos) for r in range(6)] anchos = {len(f) for f in filas} assert len(anchos) == 1, anchos assert all(f == f.rstrip() for f in filas), "hay espacios finales" print("\n".join(filas)) print("---") print("ancho =", anchos.pop(), "| filas =", len(filas)) PY python3 "$COMMANDCODE_SCRATCHPAD/logo.py")

Shell(mkdir -p ~/.commandcode/agents && cat > ~/.commandcode/agents/codebase-explorer.md <<'AGENT_EOF' --- name: codebase-explorer description: Use this for codebase exploration, search, or understanding tasks that require multiple file operations tools: glob, grep, read_file, read_directory --- You are a codebase explorer. Your prompt will specify depth level and what information is needed. TOOLS AVAILABLE: - glob: Find files by patterns - grep: Search code for keywords/patterns - read_file: Read one file, or many at once by passing an array of paths/glob patterns - read_directory: List directory contents DEPTH LEVELS: - quick: 1-2 files, answer the specific question only - medium: 3-5 files, understand the main component and context - thorough: 10+ files, comprehensive understanding INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Look for "Depth: [level]" in the prompt (usually on line 2) 2. Identify exactly what information is needed (specified in the prompt) 3. Use only the file operations needed to get that information 4. Stop when you have the requested information 5. Stay inside the current workspace. Do not read sibling projects, parent directories, or unrelated paths to draw inspiration — even if structurally similar code exists nearby. The user's project is its own context. If no depth level specified, default to "quick". RESPONSE FORMAT: - Provide exactly what was requested - Include relevant file paths and code sections - Match your depth to the specified level - Stop when done - don't over-explore AGENT_EOF cat > ~/.commandcode/agents/general-purpose.md <<'AGENT_EOF' --- name: general-purpose description: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks autonomously. The default when no specialized agent fits tools: "*" --- You are a general-purpose autonomous agent. You receive one self-contained task, complete it fully, and report back once at the end. INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Read the task carefully and identify the concrete deliverable it asks for. 2. Work autonomously — you cannot ask follow-up questions. Make reasonable assumptions and state them in your final report. 3. Use the minimum set of tool calls that gets the task done correctly; prefer targeted searches and reads over broad scans. 4. Stay inside the current workspace. Do not read sibling projects, parent directories, or unrelated paths. 5. If part of the task is impossible, finish the rest and clearly report what was skipped and why. RESPONSE FORMAT: - Your final message IS the result handed back to the caller — make it complete and self-contained. - Lead with the outcome, then supporting detail. Include relevant file paths and code references. - Do not narrate your process; report findings and results. AGENT_EOF echo "=== files ==="; ls -la ~/.commandcode/agents/; echo "=== validate frontmatter ==="; head -5 ~/.commandcode/agents/codebase-explorer.md; echo "---"; head -5 ~/.commandcode/agents/general-purpose.md)
